exposure: preventive nursing (including measures to prevent bronchopulmonary dysplasia, circulatory disorders, pulmonary hypertension, pneumothorax, intra-ventricular hemorrhage, and ventilator-related pneumonia)
outcome: incidence of complications (bronchopulmonary dysplasia, circulatory disorders, pulmonary hypertension, pneumothorax, intra-ventricular hemorrhage, ventilator-related pneumonia)
cohort: The study included 114 neonates diagnosed with respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) who were admitted to the hospital for mechanical ventilation.
finding: The application of preventive nursing in NRDS patients receiving mechanical ventilation significantly decreased complications, reduced the amount of pulmonary surfactant, shortened the time of mechanical ventilation, reduced costs, improved clinical prognosis, and increased family member satisfaction.
